messages:
Aisha Chen: seeing intermittent packet drops between training pods in west-gpu pool. symptoms: 0.5-3% packet loss, spikes ~every 7-12m for 30-60s. flows are east-west pod->pod (same AZ). affected: tf-train-*/rank0 replicas. any ideas?
Samir Patel: saw retransmits in app metrics, also qdisc tx drops on a few nodes. is this geneve or vxlan?
Linh Tran: we run geneve overlay on the cluster for GPU pools. can you `ssh` to one of the affected nodes and paste `ip -s link show geneve0` and `ethtool -S geneve0`?
Aisha Chen: quick paste from gpu-west-12 (trimmed):
```
# ip -s link show geneve0
3: geneve0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    RX: bytes 123456789 packets 98765 errors 0 dropped 14 overruns 0 frame 0
    TX: bytes 987654321 packets 123456 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0 carrier 0 collisions 0
```
Samir Patel: dropped 14 RX on encap interface during the sample window. that points to encap processing at host level, not the pod veth. can you also `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` on the node?
Aisha Chen: ran `tc -s qdisc` — qdisc looks fine but `tx_queue_drops` bumped during incident. also captured short tcpdump around spike:
```
08:22:11.123456 IP 10.0.4.12.53122 > 10.0.6.3.9090: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12789, ack 54321, win 229, length 444
08:22:11.223890 IP 10.0.6.3.9090 > 10.0.4.12.53122: Flags [R.], seq 2000, ack 12800, win 0, length 0
```
(not a full dump, but retransmits + RSTs around same time)
Jordan M.: could be MTU or offload interaction on mlx5 NICs. we had a recent calico-geneve DaemonSet rollout, any MTU changes?
Maya R.: calico-geneve was bumped yesterday — default MTU enforced to 1450 in the CNI config. however our RDMA-enabled nodes require 9000. there might be a mismatch where the kernel/driver still expects jumbo frames.
Samir Patel: that mismatch + GSO/GRO offload toggles can cause weird fragmentation and drops on encap. check `ethtool -k` and `ip link` on the NIC.
Aisha Chen: output from `ethtool -k mlx5_core0` (trimmed):
```
GSO: on
GRO: on
 tso: off
 geneve-encap-offload: on
```
some nodes show `tso: off` and others `tso: on`. inconsistent state across the fleet.
Linh Tran: inconsistent offload state is suspicious. also check `dmesg | grep -i mlx5` for hardware errors during spikes. I've seen firmware/kernel combos where page faults + offload toggling lead to packet drops on encapsulated flows.
Aisha Chen: `dmesg` snippet from gpu-west-12: "mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: PF0 - UAR page fault on async completion" around 08:22:10 — matches spike.
Jordan M.: plan: 1) roll a quick canary to force MTU=1400 + disable GSO/GRO on geneve interface in the training namespace via a privileged daemonset; 2) drain/upgrade any nodes with firmware/kernel mismatch; 3) collect pcap at both geneve0 and physical NIC for correlation.
Samir Patel: we should also add a temporary routing fallback: pin critical training jobs to nodes with `node.kubernetes.io/ml-type=dedicated` (those have validated firmware).
Maya R.: I'll prepare a small DaemonSet manifest to set `ip link set dev geneve0 mtu 1400` and `ethtool -K geneve0 gro off gso off tso off` for the namespace.
Aisha Chen: starting canary: applying DS to 3 canary nodes now. enabling packetbeat for pod network flows. OpsBot: Canary deployment triggered on 3 nodes at 1901234580.
OpsBot: kernel-livepatch applied to gpu-west-13 at 1901234585 (automated).
Aisha Chen: initial results after ~3m: drops reduced from 1.8% -> 0.12% on the canary nodes. still monitoring cluster-wide. will escalate to incident if spikes return.
Jordan M.: if canary holds, schedule fleet-wide config enforcement + node firmware audit. we should also add prober in rouge: periodic iperf/icmp between pod pairs to catch regressions.
Samir Patel: agree — also add alert on geneve RX drop rate > 0.5% sustained for 2m.
Aisha Chen: noted. thanks all — will update when canary reaches 30m or if it regresses. :thumbsup:
